Full structure layouts for controller state, posted descriptors and CPU sets are not shown.

findings.text: This lane provides register and end of interrupt operations for the local interrupt controller through a replaceable back end, plus combined helpers for the command register pair. Callers supply an offset and, for writes, a value, with forwarding to the configured handler.

Processor to processor signalling covers one target, an arbitrary mask, mask excluding self, all excluding self, all including self, and self only. Each variant takes a vector number and, where relevant, a CPU set or number, delegating delivery to the configured back end.

Completion polling, safe polling, identifier validation and per vector bookkeeping are exposed. Safe polling yields zero when no hook exists, validation compares against a driver maximum, and bookkeeping invokes an optional hook only when present.

When the controller is not compiled in, the same names collapse to inert fallbacks: reads yield zero, writes and waits do nothing, setup does nothing, and the native completion path raises a one time warning. This preserves call sites without hardware effects.

Vector numbers map onto a strided bitmap where each group of thirty two vectors occupies a sixteen byte spaced register. Bit position is the remainder within the group and register offset scales with group index, supporting direct request and bitmap calculations.

Two predicates report interrupt state: one reads the request register for a given vector and checks its bit, the other reports pending when either that request bit or current CPU posted state indicates the vector.

Posted pending state is read from the current CPU descriptor bitmap. One build validates that the vector lies in the external range and warns once on violation, returning false; the other build always reports not pending.
The vector space holds two hundred fifty six entries with thirty two vectors per register, defining eight registers for full coverage.
Highest set search walks the bitmap from the top group downward, examining each thirty two bit word and returning the global index of its topmost set bit, or negative one when all words are clear.
Find last set returns the zero based position of the highest set bit in a machine word, using compile time evaluation for constants and a hardware bit scan otherwise.

Helpers access a mapped register block by byte offset for thirty two bit values and by combined sixty four bit access limited to the command register, plus bitmap operations that locate a vector bit through group mapping and clear, set or test it.
Trampoline physical low part is at 0x467 and high part at 0x469.

Reading the local identifier fetches the identifier register then translates it through a driver hook; without the controller it yields zero. A wakeup callback type takes an identifier and start address and returns status, while OEM check, 64 bit probe and SMT update are inert defaults.
Default physical bases are 0xfec00000 for the input output unit and 0xfee00000 for the local unit, with an input output slot size of 1024 bytes.

Delivery encodings assign fixed zero, lowest priority one, SMI two, NMI four, INIT five and external seven. Identifier offset is 0x20, version offset 0x30 with mask 0xFF00FF and directed EOI at bit 24; version is low byte and max LVT is bits 23 to 16. Integrated detection checks low nibble or always true by build.

Core register offsets include task priority 0x80, arbitration 0x90, processor priority 0xA0, completion 0xB0 with ack zero, remote read 0xC0, logical destination 0xD0, destination format 0xE0, spurious vector 0xF0, service base 0x100 with eight words, trigger 0x180, request 0x200, error 0x280 and CMCI 0x2f0.

Priority masks keep low byte, logical destination uses top byte with all CPUs 0xFF, destination format offers cluster 0x0FFFFFFF and flat 0xFFFFFFFF, spurious enables directed EOI at bit 12 focus disable at bit 9 and unit enable at bit 8, and error bits cover send and receive checksum, accept, illegal vector and illegal register encodings.

Command register is at 0x300 with high half at 0x310. Destination shorthand uses 0x40000 self, 0x80000 all including self and 0xC0000 all excluding self; receive status, level, assert, busy, logical versus physical, delivery variants, vector mask and destination field shift by 24 are defined.

Local table offsets span timer 0x320 through error 0x370 with self signalling at 0x3F0, timer initial 0x380 current 0x390 divide 0x3E0. Timer modes, mask, level, remote state, polarity, pending, delivery extraction, fixed NMI external modes and divide encodings from 1 to 128 are specified.

Extended features live at 0x400, control at 0x410, specific completion at 0x420, enable at 0x480 and per entry slots at 0x500 plus sixteen times index with at most four entries. Local mapping derives from the fixed slot; base MSR is 0x800, second ID MSR is 0x802, with enable bits 11 and 10; version and extended space predicates test threshold and high bit.

Topology limits have two builds: sixty four input output units with two hundred fifty six local units, or one hundred twenty eight input output units with thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty eight local units.

Cluster decoding uses a four bit CPU field, deriving CPU and cluster masks, extracting cluster, cluster identifier and CPU identifier portions, and computing cluster count from the invalid identifier sentinel.
Invalid identifier sentinel is 0xFF in one build and 0xFFFF in the other.
Segment handling around BIOS calls either saves data and extra segments, clears four segment registers and later restores the saved pair, or expands to nothing depending on build.

Two BIOS entry helpers perform a far call through the BIOS entry with function and input values, preserving caller state and returning register outputs; the full form returns five outputs while the simple form returns one output plus a carry derived error flag.

Population count prefers a hardware instruction when the feature is present and falls back to software otherwise, with narrow forms masking to sixteen or eight bits. Sixty four bit count either sums two thirty two bit halves or uses a single sixty four bit hardware operation by build, with register constraints differing by word size.
Random retry bound is ten attempts.

Seed acquisition executes the hardware seed instruction storing success and value, and a wrapper yields at most one word only when a positive length was requested, the seed feature is enabled and the instruction succeeds.

Assembly emission helpers have dual spellings for C inline versus pure assembly contexts, plus width selectors that choose between 32 bit and 64 bit forms for instructions, registers, pointers, alignment, byte emission and address relativity.
Sized operation aliases cover move, increment, decrement, add, subtract, exchange add and multiply, with word size register names for accumulator through destination index.
Argument register mapping follows 32 bit convention with three registers and narrow views in one build, and 64 bit convention with six registers plus quad, long, word and byte views in the other.

Probe exclusion either records the entry in a blacklist section with proper alignment or does nothing by build. An exception table helper validates a named register against both 64 bit and 32 bit lists and encodes type plus index, with a counterpart to remove the helper, and a comma helper aids variadic expansion.

Three safety guards exist: native completion without hardware warns once, posted query warns once and fails safe on out of range vectors, and sixty four bit register access is compile time limited to the command register.
Each header defines a unique inclusion guard macro to prevent double processing.
